concepts.def: Formed from alkene monomers joining without loss of atoms; e.g. poly(ethene), poly(propene).
Polymers formed with elimination of a small molecule (usually H₂O or HCl); e.g. polyester, polyamide.
Made by reacting a diol with a dicarboxylic acid; e.g. PET from ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.
Made from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid (or diacyl chloride); e.g. nylon-6,6 and Kevlar.
Condensation polymers can be hydrolysed (esters/amides break), but addition polymers are largely non-biodegradable.
Polymers can be recycled, incinerated for energy or used as feedstock for cracking, depending on type.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Polymers & Synthesis — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Polymers & Synthesis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Polymers & Synthesis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
